narrative:

Surprisingly, having no previous failures was the strongest element pulling the prediction toward passing. Your clear ambition to continue studying beyond high school also pushed the outcome in a positive direction. However, these encouraging signals were outweighed by your high amount of free time after school, which was the key factor driving the model toward predicting failure.

Compared with students who passed, you report noticeably more free time and more school absences (eight days versus an average of under four). The combination of ample unstructured time and missed classes appears to have created a pattern the model associates with lower final performance.

To improve, consider using some of that free time for structured study, even if only an extra hour or two per week. Reducing absences and turning your strong motivation for higher education into consistent daily effort could quickly shift your trajectory. Taking the remedial courses seriously is a good first step toward building those habits now.
